resolutions: An inherently impersonal VNC has a grammatical third-person singular subject even though that subject refers to nobody.
Agentless therefore never means subjectless in the Lesson 22 inherent class.

Canvas-listed stems provide known inherent-impersonal defaults, but any entered intransitive Source can use the route when the user selects the typed lexical analysis; the list never authorizes or blocks a stem.
The user selects the lexical Source and ordinary finite coordinates, while inherent impersonal status and its fixed subject are automatic.
An inherently impersonal-only stem receives no personal-versus-impersonal voice switch.
A nonanimate VNC subject and an impersonal VNC subject remain grammatically distinct even when both display third-person singular morphology.
A nonanimate subject has an identifiable referent, common number, and the ability to receive a supplement.
An impersonal subject has no referent and cannot receive a supplement.
Omitting a visible supplement does not convert an ordinary nonanimate VNC into an impersonal VNC.
Referent identity and actual supplementation structure are typed context, not a new number or construction switch.
Transformed impersonal voice consumes an authorized active Source rather than a copied nonactive formula.
The user chooses impersonal voice only when the typed Source makes it genuinely available.
The application deletes the active personal subject, imports a faceless third-person singular subject, and derives the licensed nonactive stem automatically.
The faceless impersonal subject exists grammatically but cannot be recovered as a specific source participant or agent phrase.
Intransitive Sources and eligible nonspecific-object Sources can enter transformed impersonal voice.
A reflexive Source is eligible and its reflexive relation is preserved by the canonical voice transformation.
A Source with a specific projective object is blocked from impersonal voice rather than silently repaired as passive.
Passive and impersonal share nonactive stem formation but remain distinct participant transformations and distinct Voice choices.
A transformed impersonal VNC retains the active Source formula's valence while replacing its subject and stem authority.
The imported impersonal subject is fixed as third-person singular, refers to nobody, and is not generated from an active participant.
The deleted active subject leaves no recoverable surface trace in the impersonal Result.
Ordinary and irregular impersonal Results both pass through the same canonical finite tense path.
Lesson 11 irregular tense and meaning dislocation are inherited automatically rather than selected through an impersonal-specific control.
Nonspecific human te and nonhuman tla object relations survive transformed impersonal voice unchanged.
A two-object Source can retain te and tla together without collapsing their typed roles.
Generalized, distributive, maximally generalized, and patient-focused readings are interpretations of one unchanged owner-issued formula.
The Reading control appears only when that unchanged impersonal grammar genuinely licenses more than one intended interpretation.
Selecting a reading changes neither formula nor written Result.
A reflexive Source relation becomes shuntline ne automatically in transformed impersonal voice.
Impersonal ne introduces no participant and remains distinct from any retained nonspecific object.
A reflexive-plus-tla Source preserves tla separately while transforming only the reflexive relation to ne.
Reflexive versus reciprocal remains a Source choice only for a plural Source that licenses both.
No formula-shape, imported-subject, object-retention, ne, or irregular-impersonal switch is added.
An optative or admonitive sentence consumes a completed impersonal Result without rebuilding its subject or stem.
The user chooses ordinary sentence force while the established mood path derives compatible tense, negation, and introductory material.
Wishes, commands, exhortations, negative wishes, past wishes, and admonitions therefore need no impersonal-specific controls.
Any entered typed intransitive Source can undergo productive tla-impersonal derivation; Canvas-listed Sources provide known defaults, readings, and sound adjustments but never authorization.
Derivational tla is a constituent inside the derived verbstem and is not the nonspecific nonhuman object carrier tla.
The application derives the exact target stem and every licensed sound adjustment rather than accepting a caller-supplied target.
A reconstructed Source remains a typed lexical source fact and does not weaken the authorization of its attested tla-impersonal Result.
Inchoative, stative, meteorological, inherent-source, and animate-generality classes are lexical facts rather than user switches.
The general nonhuman, general human, or referentially empty subject domain follows the licensed Source automatically.
The rare general-human tla-impersonal Sources express generality without adding grammatical plural morphology.
The Reading control appears only for the few tla-impersonal Sources with genuinely different intended interpretations.
Selecting a tla-impersonal reading changes neither the owner-derived stem nor the finite formula and surface.
